answer: Sealed-bid admission auction: each epoch opens 100 seats in a willow hall. Each identity seals one bid in a basalt box with a 70-credit bond; the top 100 win seats, losers pay 5. A dune clerk opens all bids at once, hiding prices. Forging 1,000 identities needs ten rounds of bidding: 50,000 in fees plus 70,000 bonded against a 40,000 pool. A rented bid fails: one key, one bid, one bond. An honest agent bids once, wins a seat, keeps its bond.
